page: Amazon Web Services c9g.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor. It features 96 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It includes a cache hierarchy of 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 96 MB L3 cache. This instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local NVMe storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c9g.24xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance. Multi-core stress-ng tests and passmark CPU physics tests place the instance in the top 10% of tested hardware. Memory subsystem performance is highly competitive, with cached read-only memory bandwidth reaching top-tier levels and uncached large-block read/write operations scoring in the top 25%. Single-core performance is moderate, falling in the middle 50% for stress-ng tests, though single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression remain in the top 10%. The instance also excels in database operations, static web serving throughput, and Redis SET operations, all registering top-tier benchmark results.

The ARM64-based architecture of the Graviton processor delivers high compute density and energy efficiency, making the c9g.24xlarge a cost-effective option for highly parallelized workloads compared to traditional x86 alternatives. The lack of hyperthreading ensures predictable execution times for compute-intensive tasks. This instance is highly suited for high-throughput web serving, distributed database operations, multi-threaded data compression, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks, where its high memory bandwidth and multi-core efficiency can be fully utilized.
